policy: Every registered Lotus repository must use LOTUS_AUTOMERGE_TOKEN for rebase auto-merge and must dispatch main-releasability.yml through an immutable merge-SHA ref after merged PRs. Exceptions are temporary rollout records, not permanent approval.

exceptions.reason: lotus-idea main dispatches through a typed program (scripts/main_releasability_dispatch.py) that preserves every governed semantic (rebase-only assertion, merge-SHA-anchored enumeration with count equality, immutable tag refs, per-revision expected_sha) but the validator only inspects workflow shell literals and cannot verify script-based dispatchers yet.

lotus-workbench main (883899e2) dispatches through scripts/dispatch-main-releasability.mjs, so the workflow run block holds no shell literals for the validator to inspect and it reports the governed semantics as absent. Read by hand on 2026-09-08: all three violations are false. The script passes expected_sha per enumerated revision; lotus-workbench main-releasability.yml checks out ref: inputs.expected_sha, so the exact revision is built and no immutable tag ref is needed for that guarantee; and because it writes no refs, contents: read is correct least privilege rather than a missing permission -- the contents: write rule assumes tag creation, which this design deliberately avoids (a per-revision tag write is refused when the tagged commit workflow tree differs from the default branch tip, because the Actions token lacks workflows scope). Measured against origin/main, which is what the governed check evaluates; a working-tree read gives a different set. NOT covered here and raised with the owner: the script enumerates with rev-list -n commitCount, the count-bounded form tracked in lotus-platform#859. Same cause and expiry as the lotus-idea entry.
